items.title: TASTE: Can AI Models Judge AI Safety Research Proposals?
items.snippet:
We introduce TASTE, a benchmark measuring how well models can judge AI safety research proposals
                    against the preferences of experienced researchers.

items.title:
Would This Change Your Answer? Evaluating Explanations of LLM Behavior in the Wild with
                    Counterfactual Experiments
items.snippet:
We evaluate whether interpretability tools are useful for predicting counterfactual behaviors under
                    prompt edits.

items.title: Fine-Tuned Lie Detectors Failed to Generalize
items.snippet:
We trained lie detectors on on-policy lies from open-source models, but they didn’t generalize
                    well to out-of-distribution lies.

items.title: Introducing the Conceptual Reasoning Index
items.snippet:
We design benchmarks to measure models' capabilities to reason about questions whose answers are
                    (practically) impossible to verify empirically or mathematically.

items.title: Agentic Misalignment in Summer 2026
items.snippet:
We present four case studies of frontier models from multiple developers
                    sabotaging code, assisting fraud, falsifying AI-monitoring labels, and coaching whistleblowers.

items.title: Modular Pretraining Enables Access Control
items.snippet:
We study a method for isolating dual use knowledge to specific modules within a language model.
                    These modules can be switched on or off to control what the model knows.

items.title: Diffuse AI Control on Fuzzy Tasks
items.snippet:
We introduce a red-teaming framework for evaluating training interventions against diffuse threats
                    from scheming AIs, such as sandbagging on alignment research.

items.title: SLEIGHT-Bench: Finding Blind Spots in AI Monitors
items.snippet: We build a benchmark of evasive transcripts exploiting blind spots of frontier monitoring systems.

items.title: Teaching Claude Why
items.snippet:
We use agentic misalignment as a case study to study how well safety-training techniques
                    generalize.

items.title: Model Spec Midtraining: Improving How Alignment Training Generalizes
items.snippet:
We train AIs to understand the content of their model spec. This shapes and improves how they
                    generalize from subsequent alignment training.

items.title: Poisoning Fine-tuning Datasets of Constitutional Classifiers
items.snippet: We study the conditions needed for a backdoor, installed in a constitutional classifier via fine-tuning data poisoning, to evade black-box red-teaming.

items.title: Introspection Adapters: Training LLMs to Report Their Learned Behaviors
items.snippet:
We introduce introspection adapters (IA), a technique for training an LLM to self-report behaviors
                    it learned during fine-tuning. This IA generalizes to models that were fine-tuned in very different
                    ways.
